record.original_question: A p-adic normed space is called Hilbertian if every one-dimensional linear subspace has an orthogonal complement. Is every cartesian normed space Hilbertian?

evidence.quote: A \(p\)-adic normed space is called Hilbertian if every one-dimensional linear subspace has an orthogonal complement. The authors state that it is not known whether every cartesian normed space is Hilbertian.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K be a non-archimedean (complete) valued field with non-trivial valuation |·|, and let E be a normed K-vector space (a "p-adic normed space"); thus the norm satisfies the strong triangle inequality ‖x+y‖ ≤ max(‖x‖,‖y‖).

Two vectors x, y ∈ E are called orthogonal if ‖αx + βy‖ = max(‖αx‖, ‖βy‖) for all α, β ∈ K. More generally, two subspaces M, N ⊆ E are orthogonal if ‖m + n‖ = max(‖m‖, ‖n‖) for all m ∈ M and n ∈ N. A closed subspace N ⊆ E is called an orthogonal complement of a closed subspace M ⊆ E if E = M ⊕ N (algebraic direct sum) and M, N are orthogonal in the above sense.

Call E Hilbertian if every one-dimensional linear subspace of E admits an orthogonal complement.

A normed K-vector space E is called cartesian if it is isomorphic, as a normed space, to a finite or countable orthogonal direct sum of one-dimensional normed K-spaces — equivalently, E possesses an orthogonal base, i.e. a (Schauder) base (e_i)_{i∈I} such that for every finitely supported family of scalars (α_i) one has ‖Σ α_i e_i‖ = max_i ‖α_i e_i‖.

Question: Is every cartesian normed K-space Hilbertian? That is, if E has an orthogonal base, must every one-dimensional subspace of E possess an orthogonal complement?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches in non-archimedean functional analysis (van Rooij, Schikhof and successors) discuss Hilbertian/Cartesian p-adic normed spaces and note known subtleties (e.g. a maximal cartesian subspace of c_0 need not have an orthogonal base), but no source located explicitly resolves the question of whether every cartesian normed space is Hilbertian. Status is therefore inconclusive from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Non-Archimedean Functional Analysis (van Rooij)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference for orthogonality, cartesian and Hilbertian notions in p-adic normed spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the framework but does not record a resolution of the cartesian-implies-Hilbertian question.

status_evidence.title: W. H. Schikhof — research works
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work on orthogonal bases in p-adic spaces, including pathologies of cartesian subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Later literature exposes obstructions in cartesian p-adic spaces but no located item answers the Hilbertian question.
